[0] everyday_reading (E): In everyday lists the last number written is part of the data. A sentinel such as 99999 is a stop marker, not data, so it must not be summed or counted.
[1] misconception (M) -> SentinelProcessed: wrong rule: The sentinel value (e.g. 99999) is added to the total like the other values. Right rule: The value is tested against the sentinel before it is processed. The loop stops at the sentinel, which is never added or counted.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> SentinelProcessed: Points to LT (read, test for the sentinel, then process). An uneven trace processes before testing on the last pass, so the sentinel is included that time. (here mixing in: "The sentinel value (e.g. 999999) is added to the total like the other values")

[0] names_the_element (N): A sentinel loop is a read loop that stops when it reads a designated stop value that cannot occur as real data (the Rainfall problem).
[1] states_the_rule (S): Read a value; while it is not the sentinel, process it and read the next one. The sentinel is never processed.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): A priming read comes before the loop, then each pass runs: test value != SENTINEL, process (sum += v; count++), then read the next value at the end of the body. An equivalent form is while (true) { v = read; if (v == SENTINEL) break; process; }.
[1] output_prediction (OP): With input 3 -1 5 99999 7, keeping only non-negative values, the Rainfall average is (3+5)/2 = 4.0. The 7 after the sentinel is never read.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One pass reads one value. If it is the sentinel, the loop ends with sum and count unchanged; otherwise the (valid) value updates sum and count.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The sentinel test replaces, or is added to, the isEmpty() test. If the sentinel may be missing, keep !StdIn.isEmpty() in the condition so the program does not read past the end.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): sum (a gatherer) and count must change only for values that are not the sentinel and pass the filter. The average is computed once, after the loop.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: Soloway's sentinel-controlled running-total loop (Rainfall). Roles: sum is a gatherer, count a stepper, and the value read a most-recent holder.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> SentinelProcessed: Changing the sentinel keeps the behaviour only if the new value cannot occur in the data. Moving the test after the processing step breaks the invariant that the sentinel is never processed.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Check count > 0 before computing sum / count. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: The sentinel is the first value (count stays 0). With int operands this gives ArithmeticException (/ by zero); with a double sum it gives NaN silently.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Only values in the range of interest may be processed. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Inputs below 0 (or outside lo..hi) are added to the total because no if (t >= lo && t <= hi) guard comes before the update.
[3] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use a sentinel when the data stream marks its own end with a value outside the valid range (keyed entry with no end-of-file). If every value could be real data, use isEmpty() or a count instead.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The sentinel must appear, or the loop must also test isEmpty(). Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: The input ends without the sentinel, so the next read happens after the input is exhausted.
[5] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The sentinel must not be included in the computation. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: A process-then-test ordering adds 99999 to sum and count once.
wrong: The sentinel value (e.g. 999999) is added to the total like the other values. | right: The loop stops at the sentinel without processing it.
Sum and count are accumulators.
The sentinel loop is a read loop with its own stop value.
A sentinel loop is a while loop whose condition tests each value read against the stop value.
